name: Lohe
prior: No synthesizer, plugin, Max/Pd/Faust patch or module modelling a Rijke tube / singing flame / pyrophone was found (standard + extended). Physical instruments exist: Kastner's pyrophone (~1870, burners in glass tubes; VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrophone), Alastair Galbraith's Flame Organ (44 open glass tubes, Bunsen burners, piano keyboard; VS: rnz.co.nz ourchangingworld/546089/flame-organ), Make/Hackaday Rijke demos (pitch by tube length, sound stops if the gauze is heated from below; VS: makezine.com projects/the-flame-tube, hackaday.com/tag/rijke), Halfbakery 'Heat Organ' concept (VS: halfbakery.com Heat_20Organ). Physics: Rijke 1859, Higgins' 'singing flame'; heat source in an OPEN-ENDED tube drives a self-amplifying standing wave (thermoacoustic instability, Rayleigh criterion) (VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rijke_tube; arxiv.org/pdf/2203.06351 'Rijke tube: a nonlinear oscillator'; arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6640 'Self-oscillation'). Fire SOUND synthesis exists but is unpitched: AudioGaming AudioFire (flame/crackle/embers/gas modules, subtractive flame, granular embers; VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AudioGaming), Cornell 'Animating Fire with Sound' SIGGRAPH 2011 (combustion-model driven; VS: research.cs.cornell.edu/Sound/fire), Verron & Drettakis AES 2012 sound atoms (VS: hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00759818), garjan Rust crate fire module (VS: docs.rs/garjan), Farnell 'Designing Sound' fire practical (A: from memory, not confirmed by search), US patent 5,774,040 fire simulator. In Myzel: Hauch (noise -> bandpass, APP 3585) is the sibling; the inventor-lens 'Halm' is a jet flute.
costNotes: As specified it is native: 2 noise BufferSources + 6 BQ (feuer LP, knistern LP+HP, 3 tube bandpasses) + stutter osc + ~7 gains + WaveShaper (oversample none) = ~17 nodes -> 0.5-0.6 units (R: webaudio.md section 4, 0.03/node, Hauch L1 = 0.3 with 4 nodes); the idea's 0.8 is conservative. L3 (5 modes, 2 flames, 2 noises) ~ 1.2-1.4. BUT the honest version is a worklet: a self-oscillating tube (fractional delay line + 1-pole loss + heat-release nonlinearity with a threshold, n-tau style) measured at 0.25 units for the waveguide archetype (R: section 4) plus noise and crackle ~ 0.35 total - cheaper than the native fake AND it yields a real Rayleigh threshold, real amplitude limit cycle (the 'Stottern' emerges, no LFO) and real overblowing. Natively a feedback tube is impossible above 375 Hz because a DelayNode in a cycle is clamped to 128 frames (R: section 7), which is exactly why the native design has to crossfade noise into resonators and fake the stutter with an LFO.
soundHeld: The gesture is strong and new: hover the finger at the threshold where the tone struggles to exist, and the instrument pulses between hiss and sung tone; above it a clean hollow tone, at the top it overblows. The danger is that the native realisation is a parametric imitation: smoothstep(y) crossfading filtered noise into three Q-up-to-172 bandpasses is Hauch 'Pfeifen' with a crossfade, and a 0.8-3.3 Hz SINE tremolo on the band gains is a metronomic tremolo, whereas a real limit cycle at threshold is irregular bursting (noise-induced intermittency). Replace the sine with a relaxation/random-walk stutter (noise -> LP -> threshold) or, better, let a worklet tube do it. Physics note: a Rijke tube is open at both ends, so its modes are ALL integer harmonics, not only odd ones (odd-only is the closed-open clarinet tube) [A]; keep odd modes if the hollow timbre is wanted but do not claim it as physics - and three widely spaced odd bands (1, 3, 5 f) at Q 172 excited by noise ring like three sines with slow random amplitude: at low Rohr/Hitze the sound is a thin whistle chord, not fire. The 'Knistern' chain as written (LP 200-1000 Hz followed by HP 2 kHz on noise) passes almost nothing (-24 dB/oct on both sides with no overlap): crackle needs a dead-zone WaveShaper on the noise (curve 0 for |x| < ~0.9) or a scheduled random impulse train (Troepfchen-style). The unsung state at y below threshold is filtered noise with crackle = 'Feuer' - must carry on its own or the bottom third of the finger range is dead (the idea notes this).
soundBurst: Weak as specified: the Puls hit is 'Wumm' (150 ms LP noise thump) plus s = 1 on the tube gains for the gate. A bandpass with Q = 12 + 160*s = 172 at 200 Hz has a ring-up time of about Q/(pi f) = 0.27 s, so a 50-100 ms gate produces almost no tone - the hit is a filtered-noise kick with a faint whistle tail, i.e. Hauch burst. Fix: for bursts drop Q to ~20-30 and excite with an impulse/noise burst into the bands (ring-down instead of ring-up), or in the worklet start the tube above threshold with a 'gas shot'. Long Puls gates (Flammenorgel chords) work, because the threshold crossfade then has time.
failureModes: Third 'noise -> bandpass' engine (Hauch, Halm): the sung state at high Q is three sine-like ringers with random amplitude = Hauch 'Pfeifen'; distinction rests on crackle, threshold play and overblowing
Stutter as a sine LFO = metronomic tremolo, not thermoacoustic bursting; use a noise-driven relaxation or a true limit cycle (worklet)
Knistern chain (LP 200-1000 Hz then HP 2 kHz) is a band gap, outputs near-silence; needs a dead-zone shaper or impulse scheduler
Puls: Q ~172 bands cannot ring up inside a short gate (ring-up ~ Q/(pi f) ~ 0.27 s at 200 Hz); hits are noise thumps - lower Q and impulse excitation for bursts
Physics claim 'only odd modes' is wrong for an open-open Rijke tube (all harmonics) [A]; fine as timbre, wrong as story
Native self-oscillating tube impossible above 375 Hz (DelayNode cycle = 128 frames, R: webaudio.md section 7); the native design must stay a crossfade fake
Unsung bottom third of the finger range is plain filtered noise + crackle; must be made to carry (Glut bed, Rieseln-style motion) or the range feels dead
Bands at 3f/5f above ~8 kHz for notes above 1.5 kHz: thin; fold or limit range

Threshold position y_th = 0.45(1-Hitze) moves with the Hitze parameter and with Gestik tilt (Neigung = Hitze): the 'edge' the player hunts moves under the finger - good as a feature, confusing without a visual cue
verdict: New: nothing in synth land models a singing flame or Rijke tube (only physical pyrophones, flame organs and unpitched fire-sound tools such as AudioFire and the Cornell combustion work). Natively it is cheap (about 0.6 units, 1.3 at level 3) but it is then a parametric fake - noise crossfaded into three high-Q bandpasses with a sine tremolo - which risks being Hauch with a crossfade and a metronomic stutter; a worklet tube with a heat-release nonlinearity would be cheaper still (~0.35) and would produce the threshold, the irregular bursting and the overblow for real, which a native DelayNode loop cannot above 375 Hz. The held note has a strong, genuinely new gesture (hunting the threshold), provided the crackle chain is fixed (as written it is a band gap) and the unsung state carries. The Puls hit is weak: Q-172 resonators cannot ring up inside a short gate, so hits are noise thumps unless bursts use low Q and impulse excitation.
